lessons.name: [KAFKA-OFFSET-REWIND-2026] Rewind a Kafka consumer group to a timestamp
lessons.trigger: Use [KAFKA-OFFSET-REWIND-2026] when a Kafka consumer group must replay records from a verified timestamp without changing unrelated groups.
steps: Pause the target consumer group and record its current offsets.
Confirm the topic, partition range, replay timestamp, and retention window.
Use kafka-consumer-groups to reset only the target group to the timestamp.
Resume the group and compare lag and processed record counts with the change window.
failureModes: Resetting a production group before recording its offsets makes rollback difficult.
A timestamp older than retention resolves to no usable offset.
Resetting every group on the topic causes unrelated consumers to replay data.

lessons.name: [POSTGRES-LOCK-TIMEOUT-2026] Diagnose and safely clear a PostgreSQL lock timeout
lessons.trigger: Use [POSTGRES-LOCK-TIMEOUT-2026] when a PostgreSQL transaction is blocked by a lock and the owning session must be identified before termination.
steps: Capture the blocked PID, relation, wait event, and transaction age from pg_stat_activity and pg_locks.
Identify the blocking session and confirm it belongs to the intended application or migration.
Ask the owner to finish or cancel the transaction before using pg_cancel_backend.
Use pg_terminate_backend only after recording the impact and verifying the blocker is safe to stop.
failureModes: Killing the blocked session instead of the blocker leaves the lock in place.
Terminating an unknown long transaction can roll back valuable work.
A retry storm can recreate the lock immediately after it is cleared.

lessons.name: [REDIS-STREAM-CLAIM-2026] Recover a Redis Stream message from an idle consumer
lessons.trigger: Use [REDIS-STREAM-CLAIM-2026] when a Redis Stream consumer has left pending messages idle and another consumer must claim them safely.
steps: Inspect XPENDING for the stream and consumer group to verify the idle age and delivery count.
Confirm the original consumer is unavailable and choose a minimum idle threshold.
Use XAUTOCLAIM or XCLAIM for the bounded message range and record the new owner.
Process the messages idempotently, then acknowledge only after durable completion.
failureModes: Claiming active messages below the idle threshold creates duplicate processing.
Acknowledging before the side effect completes loses the message on a crash.
Ignoring delivery counts can hide a poison message loop.

lessons.name: [S3-MULTIPART-ABORT-2026] Abort stale S3 multipart uploads
lessons.trigger: Use [S3-MULTIPART-ABORT-2026] when incomplete S3 multipart uploads are consuming storage and must be removed without touching completed objects.
steps: List multipart uploads and filter by bucket, prefix, owner, and initiation age.
Exclude uploads inside an active retention or recovery window.
Abort each approved upload and capture the upload ID and response.
Recheck incomplete-upload storage after the lifecycle interval.
failureModes: Deleting objects instead of aborting uploads leaves multipart parts behind.
A broad prefix can remove an active upload owned by another workflow.
Skipping pagination leaves stale uploads undiscovered.

lessons.name: [DOCKER-IMAGE-DIGEST-PIN-2026] Pin a Docker deployment to an image digest
lessons.trigger: Use [DOCKER-IMAGE-DIGEST-PIN-2026] when a Docker deployment must consume an immutable image digest instead of a mutable tag.
steps: Resolve the approved tag to its registry digest and verify the platform manifest.
Record the digest, source commit, vulnerability result, and approval ticket.
Replace the deployment image reference with repository@sha256:digest.
Roll out one canary, verify the running image ID, and then complete the rollout.
failureModes: Pinning a local image ID that is absent from the registry breaks new nodes.
Changing the tag without changing the digest leaves the old artifact deployed.
A multi-architecture tag can resolve to an unintended platform.

lessons.name: [K8S-POD-ROLLBACK-2026] Roll back a Kubernetes Deployment revision
lessons.trigger: Use [K8S-POD-ROLLBACK-2026] when a Kubernetes Deployment revision causes a verified regression and the previous revision is known to be safe.
steps: Inspect rollout history, ReplicaSet health, and the first failing event.
Confirm the previous revision image and configuration are still available.
Run kubectl rollout undo for the named Deployment and watch rollout status.
Verify readiness, error rate, and dependent service behavior before closing the incident.
failureModes: Rolling back without identifying the bad revision can restore another broken version.
A stale ConfigMap can make the old image fail after rollback.
Declaring success before old pods terminate leaves mixed behavior.

lessons.name: [TERRAFORM-STATE-RECOVER-2026] Recover a Terraform state lock
lessons.trigger: Use [TERRAFORM-STATE-RECOVER-2026] when Terraform reports a stale state lock after the owning run has stopped.
steps: Check the CI run, state backend metadata, and lock owner before changing the lock.
Verify no Terraform process is still planning or applying the workspace.
Use the backend-specific force-unlock command with the exact lock ID.
Run a refresh-only plan and review drift before any apply.
failureModes: Force-unlocking a live apply permits concurrent state writes.
Using a lock ID from another workspace can damage the wrong state.
Applying immediately after unlock can hide unreviewed drift.

lessons.name: [NGINX-UPSTREAM-DRAIN-2026] Drain one NGINX upstream before maintenance
lessons.trigger: Use [NGINX-UPSTREAM-DRAIN-2026] when one NGINX upstream must stop receiving new requests while existing connections finish.
steps: Confirm the upstream address and current request and connection counts.
Mark only the target server down or drain it through the service discovery control plane.
Reload NGINX with a syntax check and observe that new requests avoid the target.
Wait for the connection drain, perform maintenance, then restore and verify traffic.
failureModes: Editing the wrong upstream can remove capacity from an unrelated service.
A hard stop drops long-lived WebSocket or upload connections.
Restoring the server before health checks pass reintroduces failures.

lessons.name: [GIT-REBASE-CONFLICT-2026] Resolve a Git rebase conflict with a clean handoff
lessons.trigger: Use [GIT-REBASE-CONFLICT-2026] when a topic branch must be rebased and conflicting files need review before the rewritten history is shared.
steps: Fetch the target base and create a safety branch pointing at the current topic tip.
Start the rebase and inspect every conflict with surrounding tests and ownership context.
Stage only reviewed resolutions, continue the rebase, and run focused checks.
Force-push with lease only after communicating the rewritten commit range.
failureModes: Using git add -A can stage unrelated generated files.
Resolving by choosing one side blindly can drop required behavior.
A plain force-push can overwrite a teammate's new commits.

lessons.name: [JWT-KEY-ROTATION-2026] Rotate JWT signing keys with overlap
lessons.trigger: Use [JWT-KEY-ROTATION-2026] when JWT signing keys must rotate while already-issued tokens remain valid during a controlled overlap.
steps: Generate the new key in the approved key store and assign a new key ID.
Publish the new public key to verifiers while retaining the old key for its token lifetime.
Switch signers to the new key and verify both key IDs across a canary.
Remove the old public key only after the maximum token lifetime and clock skew have elapsed.
failureModes: Removing the old key immediately invalidates still-valid sessions.
Reusing a key ID can make caches interpret the wrong public key.
Rotating signers before verifiers creates transient authentication failures.

lessons.name: [PROMETHEUS-RULE-SILENCE-2026] Silence a noisy Prometheus alert during maintenance
lessons.trigger: Use [PROMETHEUS-RULE-SILENCE-2026] when a known maintenance window would otherwise page on a specific Prometheus alert.
steps: Identify the exact alert name and stable labels in Alertmanager.
Create a narrowly scoped silence with an owner, reason, start, and end time.
Confirm the intended alert is silenced while unrelated alerts still route.
Remove or review the silence after maintenance and attach the maintenance result.
failureModes: Silencing by a broad instance label suppresses unrelated incidents.
An omitted expiration leaves the alert disabled indefinitely.
A silence without an owner cannot be audited or renewed safely.

lessons.name: [RABBITMQ-DLQ-REPLAY-2026] Replay selected RabbitMQ dead-letter messages
lessons.trigger: Use [RABBITMQ-DLQ-REPLAY-2026] when a bounded set of RabbitMQ dead-letter messages must be replayed after the consumer defect is fixed.
steps: Inspect the dead-letter exchange, routing key, message headers, and failure reason.
Filter the replay by message ID or time range and preserve the original payload.
Republish to the approved exchange with a replay marker and bounded rate.
Confirm successful consumption and route persistent failures back to a quarantine queue.
failureModes: Replaying the entire dead-letter queue can duplicate already-recovered work.
Omitting a replay marker makes duplicate diagnosis difficult.
Publishing before the consumer fix is deployed recreates the failure.

lessons.name: [ELASTIC-INDEX-ALIAS-SWAP-2026] Swap an Elasticsearch write alias atomically
lessons.trigger: Use [ELASTIC-INDEX-ALIAS-SWAP-2026] when a rebuilt Elasticsearch index is ready and reads or writes must move through an atomic alias change.
steps: Build and validate the new index with mappings, document counts, and sample queries.
Pause or coordinate writers so the final catch-up has a known boundary.
Use the aliases API in one atomic action to move the write and read aliases.
Resume writers, monitor errors, and retain the old index until rollback is no longer needed.
failureModes: Changing read and write aliases in separate calls creates a split-brain window.
Deleting the old index before validation removes the rollback path.
Skipping the final catch-up loses documents written during the rebuild.

lessons.name: [CI-CACHE-INVALIDATE-2026] Invalidate a CI dependency cache after a lockfile change
lessons.trigger: Use [CI-CACHE-INVALIDATE-2026] when a CI dependency lockfile changed and stale cached packages are causing reproducible build failures.
steps: Compare the lockfile hash and cache key used by the failing job.
Create a new cache key that includes the package manager and lockfile digest.
Invalidate only the affected branch or namespace and run one uncached job.
Verify the new cache is populated from the lockfile and that later jobs are reproducible.
failureModes: Deleting every organization cache increases queue time and hides the scope of the defect.
Changing the key without the lockfile digest allows stale dependencies back in.
Reusing a cache across operating systems can restore incompatible binaries.

lessons.name: [SYSTEMD-SERVICE-ROLLBACK-2026] Roll back a systemd service unit safely
lessons.trigger: Use [SYSTEMD-SERVICE-ROLLBACK-2026] when a host service unit change causes startup failure and the last known-good unit is available.
steps: Capture systemctl status, journal logs, the unit checksum, and the active package version.
Restore the last known-good unit or package from the approved artifact store.
Run systemd-analyze verify, daemon-reload, and a controlled restart.
Check readiness, dependencies, and restart count before returning the host to service.
failureModes: Editing the unit while the service is running can leave an untracked partial change.
Skipping daemon-reload tests a stale unit definition.
Restarting dependent services in the wrong order extends the outage.

lessons.name: [PYTHON-VENV-REPAIR-2026] Repair a Python virtual environment from a lock file
lessons.trigger: Use [PYTHON-VENV-REPAIR-2026] when a Python virtual environment has broken entry points and must be recreated from the committed lock file.
steps: Record the Python version, platform, failing command, and current lockfile checksum.
Move the damaged environment aside instead of deleting it immediately.
Create a fresh environment with the pinned interpreter and install from the lock file.
Run import, entry-point, and focused application checks before switching the service.
failureModes: Installing unpinned latest packages changes behavior during repair.
Deleting the old environment first removes useful forensic evidence.
Using a different Python minor version can produce incompatible wheels.

lessons.name: [HELM-VALUES-VERIFY-2026] Verify rendered Helm values before applying
lessons.trigger: Use [HELM-VALUES-VERIFY-2026] when a Helm values change needs rendered-manifest review before it reaches a shared cluster.
steps: Render the chart with the exact release, chart version, values files, and namespace.
Diff the rendered output against the last approved manifest and inspect security-sensitive fields.
Run schema and policy validation against the rendered resources.
Apply only the reviewed revision and verify the rollout against the rendered intent.
failureModes: Rendering with a different chart version invalidates the review.
Reviewing values without rendered output misses template defaults.
Applying a local override file accidentally can change unrelated resources.

lessons.name: [MYSQL-REPLICA-LAG-2026] Reduce MySQL replica lag before a read cutover
lessons.trigger: Use [MYSQL-REPLICA-LAG-2026] when MySQL replica lag threatens a read cutover and the cause must be measured before traffic moves.
steps: Measure Seconds_Behind_Source, relay backlog, apply throughput, and source write rate.
Check for long-running queries, locks, disk saturation, and replication errors.
Remove the verified bottleneck or throttle source writes during the catch-up window.
Cut over reads only after lag is zero or within the documented tolerance for two checks.
failureModes: Treating NULL lag as zero can hide a stopped SQL thread.
Increasing parallel workers without checking lock contention can worsen lag.
Cutting over during catch-up serves stale reads.

lessons.name: [CLOUDFLARE-DNS-CUTOVER-2026] Perform a staged Cloudflare DNS cutover
lessons.trigger: Use [CLOUDFLARE-DNS-CUTOVER-2026] when a Cloudflare DNS record must move to a new origin with a reversible staged cutover.
steps: Verify the new origin certificate, health endpoint, and expected Host header.
Lower the record TTL ahead of the change and document the previous record.
Change the record or weighted split in a small percentage, then check regional probes.
Increase traffic gradually and restore the previous value if error or latency thresholds fail.
failureModes: Changing DNS before the certificate is valid causes TLS failures.
Assuming a low TTL eliminates resolver caching overstates rollback speed.
A broad zone edit can change records unrelated to the service.

lessons.name: [GRPC-REFLECTION-DEBUG-2026] Debug a gRPC service with reflection
lessons.trigger: Use [GRPC-REFLECTION-DEBUG-2026] when a gRPC endpoint supports reflection and an RPC must be inspected without a generated client.
steps: Confirm the endpoint, TLS mode, authority header, and environment authorization.
Use grpcurl list and describe to inspect services and message schemas.
Invoke a read-only RPC with a minimal request and capture status metadata.
Remove debug access or disable reflection if it was temporarily enabled.
failureModes: Sending a mutating RPC during discovery can change production state.
Ignoring TLS authority settings can target the wrong virtual host.
Leaving reflection enabled exposes service schema beyond the intended window.
